result.title: Attention Temperature Confounds Zero-Shot Context Extension
result.summary: A training-time attention change is usually judged for zero-shot context extension against a dense baseline beyond the training length at the default temperature, $τ= 1$. The outcome depends on how miscalibrated the baseline is there: the share of perplexity it recovers when its logits are sharpened by one scalar. Under the standard recipe (fp32 master weights), an 8k-trained baseline is 8-15% miscalibrated at 30k in three seed-paired 365M twins; in one of them this makes the block-sparse-trained twin look 7% better, which calibration removes. In pure-bf16 training without master weights the miscalibration is several times larger: an AdamW step ($β_2 = 0.95$) on a gain initialised at 1.0 is below half the bf16 spacing at peak learning rates under $1.7\times10^{-3}$, so gains never move (22 checkpoints), the baseline is 37-58% miscalibrated, and block-sparse pretraining, attention dropout and ALiBi look 6-35% better. Calibrating one temperature per model and length removes all three advantages, leaves ALiBi 5% behind RoPE and keeps part of the gain of a positive control, NTK-aware scaling. Unfreezing the gains reverses the block-sparse advantage at 365M and removes 71-89% of it at 1.2B. We recommend reporting extension results at calibrated temperatures and checking that normalisation gains moved.

AI.brief_summary: 论文考察训练期注意力改动（block-sparse attention、attention dropout、ALiBi）在零样本上下文外推评测中受 temperature 失校准混淆的问题：用种子配对的 365M/1.2B 模型，按模型与长度分别校准 temperature 后重做比较，发现原本 6–35% 的优势大多消失，并指出 bf16 训练下归一化 gain 几乎不动会放大失校准。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文不涉及视觉或 latent 推理，但其「先校准温度、确认 gain 是否更新」的评测诊断线索可供核查：若在 LVR 中比较稀疏注意力、位置编码或缓存/注意力结构改动，类似未校准差异可能被误读为结构收益。
